Q: Installed Text-To-Speech Voices Not Showing Up in System.Speech Options, Windows 10 Powershell A:

The easiest way to copy them from one key path to another is to export the keys from HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Speech_OneCore\Voices\Tokens\

Then open the .reg file in notepad, replace the path HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Speech_OneCore\Voices\Tokens\ with HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Speech\Voices\Tokens, resave it then double click the .reg file to import it back into your registry.

Q: Pass field names into function-based validators A:

I can't test it but the simplest could be to use lambda to send extra parameter field

Original function need extra parameter

def validate_string(value, field):  # <-- field
    # if not isinstance(value, str):
    if type(value) is not str:
        raise ValidationError(_("field.string").format(field=field), code="invalid")

and later

self.fields["email"].validators = [lambda value: validate_string(value, "email")]

In documentation for validators you can find links to source code e.g. EmailValidator and you may see how to use class to set extra parameters and how to use __call__ to run validation.

Probably something like this (with self.field)

class MyStringValidator:

    def __init__(self, field):
        self.field = field

    def __call__(self, value):
        # if not isinstance(value, str):
        if type(value) is not str:
            raise ValidationError(_("field.string").format(field=self.field), code="invalid")

and

self.fields["email"].validators = [MyStringValidator("email")]

Q: PIL Image ImportError A:

This is an issue with your installation: Image module have been installed as subpackage of a PIL module, while the library you are using expects Image module to be directly in the python path. Simplest solution is to replace:

import Image

with:

from PIL import Image

in file qrcode/image/pil.py.

Q: How can I prevent multiple instances of a class from being created? A:

The task is underspecified. Which aspects of the given code are you allowed to change? A typical Singleton is designed to prevent creation via API design, i.e. the class itself creates an instance and keeps it and only provides an API to access it. This, however, would be a very drastic change to the given class. Most notably, Singletons do not work with a constructor taking parameters. Having a parameter means, you can have different callers with different values which is the kind of error, the API design of a Singleton should not allow.

The other approach, taking the task literally, would not change the API but insert a mechanism to prevent creating a second instance, like a static flag which is set on the first constructor execution and a check which will throw an exception on every attempt to execute the constructor again.
Since this doesn’t change the API, there still can be multiple attempts, even with different constructor parameters, but there will be only one winner in this case.
The preferred implementation of such a flag would use an atomic check-and-set operation, to ensure the requirement in all scenarios, including multi-threaded creation attempts.
